correctness.rationale: Normalize nonzero inputs by the sum of squared radii. For d=N−1 assign to each of the N sign rows a norming coordinate; two rows collide. Both the agree and disagree sets of signs are nonempty, so the two scalar sums A±B satisfy |A+B||A−B|=|A²−B²|≤(R−t)² with R the sum and t the minimum radius. All other factors are ≤R. Cauchy–Schwarz on the remaining m radii with sum S yields exactly F_n(z)=m^q(m+z)^(2−q)/(m+z²), z=mt/S∈[0,1]. Its derivative has the sign of (2−q)m−2mz−qz², strictly decreasing with opposite endpoint signs, giving the claimed z_n. For the witness, keep one full signed coordinate for each row except a pair differing only in the last sign, and give that pair a shared coordinate omitting the last component. For either omitted row at each other coordinate the first m sign products match at index one and disagree at least once, so their absolute sum is ≤m−2; adding z_n≤1 cannot exceed m. Thus the omitted norms are m and all other norms m+z_n. Saturation is attained with one coordinate per row, and conversely compactness gives an attaining tuple; equality in Cauchy–Schwarz and the scalar triangle inequality forces equal positive radii and a different norming coordinate for each row modulo global reversal. The root equation gives 1−z_n=O(q); near 1 the log derivative at 1 is O(q/n) and its derivative O(1/n), yielding F_n(z_n)−F_n(1)=O(q²). Now F_n(1)=n(1−1/n)^q and n log(n/(n−1))→1, proving the deficit asymptotic. Independent decimal evaluation of the n=4 witness gives 3.532200615298932666… .
residual_risks: The collision uses real scalar factorization. No general lower-dimension formula or complete maximizing-tuple classification is asserted.

value.rationale: The last dimension before saturation is selected by the sign-cube geometry, not by numerical convenience. Quantifying the exact cost of losing one norming coordinate for every order and showing the deficit is asymptotic to 4/N provide a usable benchmark for comparing geometric versus arithmetic signed-sum invariants. The simple shared-coordinate construction explains why a tailored unequal-radius witness is needed instead of an equal-radius estimate.
residual_risks: The value is in the all-orders penultimate law; the method, the invariant's definition and the broader saturation idea are not presented as new in isolation.
